For the purposes of this analysis, we evaluate two ‘bookend’ scenarios to highlight this dynamic range: (1) a high RG yield scenario and (2) a high alcohol yield scenario. For the remainder of the report these two scenarios will be denoted as the HighRG and HighAlc cases. It should be stressed that all analysis and modelling was based on previous experimental work provided by West Biofuels and all flows around the mixed alcohol synthesis (MAS) reactor were used verbatim with respect to inlet, recycle, and product compositions and flow rates. Any uncertainties or idiosyncrasies in the provided data are propagated through the analyses. General plant design and operating assumptions are, unless stated otherwise herein, based on previous NREL mixed alcohol reports [1]. Consequently, with many of the key process areas being identical to those in prior reports, in the following sections we use excerpts of existing language verbatim or in a summarized form. 10 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nrel.gov/publications. 2.1 Experimental West Biofuels Data Experimental data for the HighRG and HighAlc cases were provided by West Biofuels corresponding to the MAS flow diagram shown in Figure 1.
